title: The past: regular preterite
objectives: I can say what I did yesterday and last weekend using regular verbs in the past.
I can form the pretérito perfeito of regular -ar, -er and -ir verbs for every person, including a gente and eles.
I can spell the eu form of verbs ending in -car, -çar and -gar correctly (toquei, comecei, paguei).
I can ask and answer questions about past events and say what I did not do.
I can place events in time with ontem, anteontem, a semana passada, há dois dias and faz um mês.

example.pt: Ontem eu trabalhei até tarde.
example.en: Yesterday I worked until late.

example.pt: Anteontem choveu o dia inteiro.
example.en: The day before yesterday it rained all day.

vocabulary.note: Usually used with na: na semana passada. The same pattern works for o mês passado and o ano passado.

example.pt: Na semana passada eu visitei meus avós.
example.en: Last week I visited my grandparents.

example.pt: No mês passado meu irmão mudou de emprego.
example.en: Last month my brother changed jobs.

vocabulary.note: Há plus a period of time means 'ago'. It is written with an accent and an h, exactly like the existential há.

example.pt: Comprei este celular há três meses.
example.en: I bought this phone three months ago.

vocabulary.note: Very common in everyday Brazilian speech: dois dias atrás means the same as há dois dias.

example.pt: Ele chegou dois dias atrás.
example.en: He arrived two days ago.

example.pt: Eu descansei o fim de semana inteiro.
example.en: I rested the whole weekend.

example.pt: A festa começou às nove da noite.
example.en: The party started at nine at night.

example.pt: A gente assistiu a um show incrível.
example.en: We watched an incredible concert.

example.pt: O jantar terminou muito tarde.
example.en: Dinner ended very late.

example.pt: Ela comemorou o aniversário num restaurante.
example.en: She celebrated her birthday in a restaurant.

example.pt: Nós comemoramos o aniversário do Pedro no sábado.
example.en: We celebrated Pedro's birthday on Saturday.

example.pt: Encontrei um amigo antigo no mercado.
example.en: I ran into an old friend at the market.

example.pt: Conversamos por horas no telefone.
example.en: We talked for hours on the phone.

example.pt: Meu pai cozinhou o almoço inteiro.
example.en: My father cooked the whole lunch.

example.pt: Limpei a casa toda no sábado.
example.en: I cleaned the whole house on Saturday.

example.pt: Lavei o carro de manhã.
example.en: I washed the car in the morning.

vocabulary.note: Formally assistir takes the preposition a (assistir a um filme). In everyday speech many Brazilians drop it.

example.pt: Assistimos a um filme ontem à noite.
example.en: We watched a movie last night.

example.pt: Recebi uma mensagem da Lia.
example.en: I received a message from Lia.

example.pt: Ele vendeu o carro velho.
example.en: He sold the old car.

example.pt: Aprendi uma música nova no violão.
example.en: I learned a new song on the guitar.

example.pt: Escrevi um e-mail bem longo.
example.en: I wrote a very long email.

example.pt: Ela não respondeu a minha mensagem.
example.en: She did not answer my message.

example.pt: Abrimos a porta às oito horas.
example.en: We opened the door at eight o'clock.

vocabulary.note: Preterite: saí, saiu, saímos, saíram. The accented í marks a separate syllable.

example.pt: Saímos de casa muito cedo.
example.en: We left home very early.

example.pt: Paguei a conta do jantar.
example.en: I paid the dinner bill.

example.pt: Ele tocou violão na festa.
example.en: He played the guitar at the party.

example.pt: O show começou atrasado.
example.en: The concert started late.

example.pt: Cheguei em casa à meia-noite.
example.en: I got home at midnight.

example.pt: Esqueci o celular em casa.
example.en: I forgot my phone at home.

example.pt: A gente dançou a noite toda.
example.en: We danced all night.

dialogues.title: Monday morning news
dialogues.context: Ana and Carlos meet at the office coffee machine on Monday and compare their weekends.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Oi, Carlos! Você descansou no fim de semana?
lines.en: Hi, Carlos! Did you rest over the weekend?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Descansei pouco. No sábado eu limpei a casa toda e cozinhei pra minha mãe.
lines.en: Only a little. On Saturday I cleaned the whole house and cooked for my mother.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: E no domingo?
lines.en: And on Sunday?

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: No domingo a gente almoçou na casa da minha tia e depois assistiu a um filme.
lines.en: On Sunday we had lunch at my aunt's house and then watched a movie.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Que legal! Eu encontrei umas amigas e a gente conversou por horas num café.
lines.en: How nice! I met some friends and we talked for hours in a café.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Vocês comeram bem?
lines.en: Did you eat well?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Comemos um bolo enorme. Eu paguei a conta e elas pagaram o táxi.
lines.en: We ate an enormous cake. I paid the bill and they paid for the taxi.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.pt: Então você aproveitou mais o fim de semana do que eu!
lines.en: So you enjoyed the weekend more than I did!

dialogues.title: After the birthday party
dialogues.context: Júlia, Pedro and Marina talk the day after Marina's birthday party.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Marina, parabéns de novo! Eu adorei a festa de ontem.
lines.en: Marina, congratulations again! I loved yesterday's party.

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Obrigada! Vocês chegaram tarde, né? Eu procurei vocês a noite toda.
lines.en: Thanks! You arrived late, right? I looked for you all night.

lines.speaker: Júlia
lines.pt: Chegamos às dez. O ônibus demorou e o Pedro esqueceu o presente em casa.
lines.en: We arrived at ten. The bus took a long time and Pedro forgot the present at home.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: É verdade! Voltei pra buscar e perdi uma hora.
lines.en: True! I went back to get it and lost an hour.

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Não tem problema. Vocês chegaram bem na hora, e o show começou logo depois.
lines.en: No problem. You arrived right on time, and the show started soon after.

lines.speaker: Júlia
lines.pt: Seu primo tocou violão muito bem. Todo mundo dançou!
lines.en: Your cousin played the guitar very well. Everybody danced!

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Ele aprendeu essas músicas há um mês, só pra festa.
lines.en: He learned those songs a month ago, just for the party.

lines.speaker: Pedro
lines.pt: Gostei de tudo! Você recebeu muitos presentes?
lines.en: I liked everything! Did you receive a lot of presents?

lines.speaker: Marina
lines.pt: Recebi bastante. Abri todos hoje de manhã.
lines.en: Quite a few. I opened them all this morning.

dialogues.title: The report that did not arrive
dialogues.context: At work, Beatriz asks her colleague Rafael about an email and a report from the day before.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Rafael, você abriu o e-mail que eu mandei ontem?
lines.en: Rafael, did you open the email I sent yesterday?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Ainda não abri. Desculpa, ontem eu trabalhei fora o dia todo.
lines.en: Not yet. Sorry, yesterday I worked out of the office all day.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Tudo bem. E o relatório? Você terminou?
lines.en: That is fine. And the report? Did you finish it?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Terminei, mas não enviei. Esqueci de mandar antes de sair.
lines.en: I finished it, but I did not send it. I forgot to send it before leaving.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: A que horas você saiu do escritório?
lines.en: What time did you leave the office?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Saí às sete. Mas eu te mando agora, de manhã.
lines.en: I left at seven. But I will send it to you now, this morning.

lines.speaker: Beatriz
lines.pt: Perfeito. Você respondeu o cliente também?
lines.en: Perfect. Did you reply to the client as well?

lines.speaker: Rafael
lines.pt: Respondi anteontem. Ele gostou da proposta.
lines.en: I replied the day before yesterday. He liked the proposal.

grammar.title: The regular preterite: -ar, -er and -ir
grammar.explanation:
The pretérito perfeito (preterite) describes a completed action at a definite moment in the past: Ontem eu comprei pão. Take the infinitive, remove -ar, -er or -ir, and add the endings in the table. The -er and -ir verbs differ only in the vowel: e for -er (comeu, comemos, comeram) and i for -ir (abriu, abrimos, abriram). The exception is the eu form, where both end in -i (comi, abri).

In Brazil, você, ele, ela and a gente all take the same third person singular form (ela falou, a gente falou), and vocês, eles and elas take the -aram, -eram, -iram form. The old second person tu form (falaste) is only used in some regions and is not needed here.

Stress matters. In the eu and você forms the stress falls on the last syllable, which is why the written accents are needed in falei (fa-LEI), falou (fa-LOU) and comeu. The nós form (falamos, comemos, abrimos) looks exactly like the present tense; context and words like ontem tell you which tense it is. In speech, a gente is far more common than nós, and it avoids the ambiguity.

examples.pt: Eu falei com a minha chefe ontem.
examples.en: I spoke with my boss yesterday.

examples.pt: A gente comeu pizza no sábado.
examples.en: We ate pizza on Saturday.

examples.pt: Ela abriu a janela e respirou fundo.
examples.en: She opened the window and took a deep breath.

examples.pt: Vocês chegaram cedo hoje.
examples.en: You arrived early today.

examples.pt: Os meninos venderam todos os livros.
examples.en: The boys sold all the books.

examples.pt: Nós aprendemos muito nesse curso.
examples.en: We learned a lot in this course.

grammar.title: Spelling changes in the eu form
grammar.explanation:
Some verbs change their spelling in the eu form of the preterite so that the sound of the final consonant stays the same before the ending -ei. Verbs in -car change c to qu (tocar: toquei), verbs in -gar change g to gu (pagar: paguei), and verbs in -çar change ç to c (começar: comecei). The other persons are completely regular: ele tocou, ele pagou, ele começou.

The reason is the pronunciation. In Portuguese, c before e or i sounds like s, and g before e or i sounds like the j in measure, so toquei needs the u to keep the hard k sound, and paguei needs the u to keep the hard g sound. The letter ç never appears before e or i, so almocei is written with a plain c.

Also remember verbs like sair, whose preterite forms carry an accent on the i: saí, saiu, saímos, saíram. Here the accent only shows that the vowels are pronounced as two syllables.

examples.pt: Eu toquei violão na festa da escola.
examples.en: I played the guitar at the school party.

examples.pt: Paguei a conta e saí.
examples.en: I paid the bill and left.

examples.pt: Cheguei atrasado, mas o filme ainda não começou.
examples.en: I arrived late, but the movie had not started yet.

examples.pt: Hoje eu almocei na rua e comecei a trabalhar mais tarde.
examples.en: Today I had lunch out and started working later.

examples.pt: Ela chegou primeiro e eu cheguei depois.
examples.en: She arrived first and I arrived later.

grammar.title: Past time markers
grammar.explanation:
Time markers tell your listener when something happened. Ontem (yesterday) and anteontem (the day before yesterday) can combine with parts of the day: ontem de manhã, ontem à tarde, ontem à noite. For longer periods use a semana passada, o mês passado and o ano passado, usually with the preposition em: na semana passada, no mês passado, no ano passado.

To say 'ago', Portuguese has three patterns. Há dois dias means 'two days ago' and comes before the time. Dois dias atrás means the same and comes after the time; this form is especially common in speech. Finally, faz dois dias que followed by a verb means 'it has been two days since': Faz um mês que eu comecei o curso. The verb after que is in the preterite.

Do not confuse há (with an h and an accent, used for time) with a. Há dois dias is 'two days ago', while daqui a dois dias is 'two days from now'. These markers are a signal to use the preterite, because they point to a finished moment.

rows: it has been a month since

examples.pt: Ontem à noite eu jantei com a minha família.
examples.en: Last night I had dinner with my family.

examples.pt: Anteontem eu encontrei a Carla na rua.
examples.en: The day before yesterday I ran into Carla on the street.

examples.pt: Eles venderam a casa há cinco anos.
examples.en: They sold the house five years ago.

examples.pt: Comprei esse sofá dois meses atrás.
examples.en: I bought this sofa two months ago.

examples.pt: Faz uma semana que eu comecei a estudar inglês.
examples.en: It has been a week since I started studying English.

grammar.title: Questions and negation in the past
grammar.explanation:
Past questions do not change the verb order. For a yes or no question, say the statement with rising intonation: Você gostou do show? For information questions, put the question word first: Quando você chegou? Onde você almoçou? Com quem você conversou? Quanto você pagou? There is no helping verb like 'did' in Portuguese; the preterite verb itself carries the tense.

To make a negative sentence, put não directly before the verb: Eu não comprei nada. Double negatives are normal: Eu não encontrei ninguém and Eu não comprei nada. When the negative word comes first, não is dropped: Ninguém respondeu. Ainda não means 'not yet': Ainda não abri o e-mail.

In Brazil the natural short answer repeats the verb instead of using sim alone: Você comprou pão? Comprei. Não comprei. A full answer such as Sim, eu comprei is correct too, but sounds more formal.

examples.pt: Você gostou da festa?
examples.en: Did you like the party?

examples.pt: Quando vocês chegaram?
examples.en: When did you arrive?

examples.pt: Eu não esqueci a sua chave.
examples.en: I did not forget your key.

examples.pt: Ninguém respondeu a mensagem.
examples.en: Nobody answered the message.

examples.pt: Você pagou a conta? Paguei.
examples.en: Did you pay the bill? I did.

examples.pt: Ainda não terminei o relatório.
examples.en: I have not finished the report yet.

culture.title: Talking about the weekend
culture.text:
On Monday morning, almost every Brazilian office starts with the same question: E aí, como foi o fim de semana? Colleagues trade stories about a churrasco at a friend's house, a balada on Saturday night, or a rolê, which is a casual outing with no fixed plan. Friday evening is often greeted with sextou, a slang word that roughly means 'it is finally Friday'.

Social life revolves around food, music and family. Birthdays are a big event: it is normal to invite relatives, neighbours and old friends, to sing parabéns pra você and to cut the bolo with a lot of noise. Guests often arrive later than the time printed on the invitation, and a party that starts at nine can easily go until the early morning. That is why so many stories about the weekend begin with A gente chegou tarde, mas valeu a pena.

Another habit worth knowing is the use of a gente in storytelling. In everyday conversation, people often prefer a gente comeu, a gente dançou over nós comemos, nós dançamos because it sounds warmer and avoids the confusion with the present tense.

readings.title: O fim de semana da Camila

paragraphs.pt: No sábado de manhã, Camila acordou cedo e limpou o apartamento. Depois ela lavou a roupa e cozinhou arroz e feijão.
paragraphs.en: On Saturday morning, Camila woke up early and cleaned the apartment. Then she washed the clothes and cooked rice and beans.

paragraphs.pt: À tarde, ela encontrou duas amigas no shopping. Elas conversaram, tomaram um café e compraram um presente pro aniversário da mãe de Camila.
paragraphs.en: In the afternoon, she met two friends at the mall. They talked, had a coffee and bought a present for Camila's mother's birthday.

paragraphs.pt: À noite, Camila e as amigas assistiram a um show na praça. O cantor tocou violão e cantou músicas antigas. Todo mundo dançou.
paragraphs.en: At night, Camila and her friends watched a concert in the square. The singer played the guitar and sang old songs. Everybody danced.

paragraphs.pt: Camila voltou pra casa só à meia-noite. No domingo, ela dormiu até as dez e almoçou com a família.
paragraphs.en: Camila went back home only at midnight. On Sunday, she slept until ten and had lunch with her family.

questions.prompt: O que a Camila cozinhou no sábado?
questions.explanation: The text says she cooked arroz e feijão after washing the clothes.

questions.prompt: Who did Camila meet in the afternoon?
questions.explanation: She met duas amigas at the mall.

questions.prompt: What time did Camila get home on Saturday night?
questions.explanation: She came home só à meia-noite.

exercises.prompt: Match the time expression with its meaning

exercises.explanation: Falei is the eu form of the preterite of falar.

exercises.prompt: Qual é a forma de a gente no pretérito de comer? A gente ___ pizza ontem.
exercises.explanation: A gente takes the same verb form as ele and ela: comeu.

exercises.hint_en: Yesterday I woke up very early.
exercises.explanation: Acordar is a regular -ar verb: acordei.
Ela, you and a gente all take the -ou ending for -ar verbs.

exercises.prompt: How do you write 'I paid' in the preterite?
exercises.explanation: Verbs in -gar add a u before -ei to keep the hard g sound.

exercises.prompt_pt: Nós ___ um filme ontem à noite.
exercises.hint_en: We watched a movie last night.
exercises.explanation: The nós form of assistir is assistimos, the same as in the present. Ontem tells you it is the past.

exercises.audio_pt: Ontem eu comi pão de queijo.

exercises.prompt: What does 'Cheguei há dois dias' mean?
choices: I will arrive in two days.
I am arriving in two days.
exercises.explanation: Há plus a period of time means 'ago'.
Pagar becomes paguei in the eu form.

exercises.prompt_pt: Ela ___ o e-mail e respondeu rápido.
exercises.hint_en: She opened the email and replied quickly.
exercises.explanation: Abrir is an -ir verb: abriu for ela.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is a correct negative in the past?
exercises.explanation: Não goes directly before the verb, and the verb agrees with eu.

exercises.prompt_en: We watched a movie last night.
answers: Nós assistimos a um filme ontem à noite.
A gente assistiu a um filme ontem à noite.
Assistimos a um filme ontem à noite.
Nós assistimos um filme ontem à noite.
A gente assistiu um filme ontem à noite.
Ontem à noite nós assistimos a um filme.
Ontem à noite a gente assistiu a um filme.
exercises.explanation: Assistir is normally followed by a, but many Brazilians drop it in speech.

exercises.audio_pt: Ela esqueceu a chave em casa.
choices: She forgot the key at home.

exercises.prompt_en: I did not pay the bill.

exercises.prompt: Como se diz 'the day before yesterday'?
exercises.explanation: Ante means before, so anteontem is 'before yesterday'.
Chegar changes to cheguei to keep the hard g sound.

exercises.audio_pt: A gente dançou a noite toda.

exercises.explanation: Gostar is followed by de, which contracts with o to do.

exercises.audio_pt: Eles venderam a casa no ano passado.
choices: They painted the house last year.
They bought the house last year.
They sold the house last year.

exercises.hint_en: I forgot my phone at home.
exercises.explanation: Esquecer is an -er verb: esqueci for eu.

exercises.prompt_en: She did not answer the message.
exercises.explanation: Responder can take the object directly, or with a in formal writing.
